capture.final_message:
Use the evaluation representation of signed/vector measures on measurable sets.

- For the first conjunct, evaluate the subtraction pointwise at \(i\). Subtraction of signed measures is inherited pointwise from vector measures, and for measurable \(i\),
  \[
  \mu.toSignedMeasure(i)=\mu.real(i).
  \]
  Thus evaluation immediately becomes \(\mu.real(i)-\nu.real(i)\).

- For the second conjunct, apply extensionality for vector measures and evaluate both sides on an arbitrary measurable set \(t\). Using measurability of \(s\),
  \[
  (\mu.toSignedMeasure.restrict\,s)(t)
  =\mu.toSignedMeasure(t\cap s)
  =\mu.real(t\cap s),
  \]
  while
  \[
  ((\mu.restrict\,s).toSignedMeasure)(t)
  =(\mu.restrict\,s).real(t)
  =\mu.real(t\cap s).
  \]

The essential assumptions are finiteness, which makes `toSignedMeasure` and the real-valued measure evaluations available, and measurability of the relevant sets, which enables the evaluation and restriction formulas.
